problems.title: The printed second difference drops a sign-relevant remainder
problems.source_location: Theorem 3.6, Claim 3.7 and Proposition 3.8, p.6; Appendix A.3, p.14
claim: Theorem 3.6 prints \(\Delta^2E_t=p_t[\Delta V_{t+1}-\Delta V_t+V_t(\epsilon_t-\epsilon_{t+1})]\). Its proof discards products of small terms without retaining a remainder or a quantitative condition controlling their effect on curvature.
analysis: Use an absorbing incorrect state, horizon \(3\), correct-proposal error \(q=0.01\), beam width \(1\) and two independent expansions. Correct proposals score \(0.5\); an incorrect proposal scores \(1\) with probability \(a_t\), otherwise \(0\). Then \(\epsilon_t=q^2+2q(1-q)a_t\), \(V_t=(1-q)^{3-t}\), \(p_{t+1}=p_t(1-\epsilon_t)\), and \(E_t=p_tV_t\). For \(\epsilon=(0.002,0.00208,0.00216)\), all ranking error rates are below random-selection error \(q\) and increase over time. Yet \[E=(0.970299,0.9781398,0.9859649184)\] has \(\Delta^2E_0=-0.0000156816\), whereas the printed right side is \(+0.00002137608\). The omitted remainder \(-0.00003705768\) reverses the sign.

Increasing errors \((0.002,0.00201,0.00202)\) instead give positive actual curvature \(0.0000534798\); increasing ranking error alone does not imply concavity. The paper’s additional dominance expectation is qualitative, so this does not refute a separately imposed numerical dominance inequality. Claim 3.7 says “we expect,” Proposition 3.8 says “typically,” the footnote calls the shapes conjectural, and Section 4 calls the stopping rule heuristic.
result: The finite equality is false and cannot alone certify curvature. The affine z-score observation and elementary concave-sequence lemma are unaffected; no new beam-search benchmark result is asserted.
assumptions: The example uses independent proposals and an absorbing incorrect state; scores implement the declared selection error probabilities.
repair: In this absorbing submodel the exact identity is \[\Delta^2E_t=p_t[(1-\epsilon_t)(1-\epsilon_{t+1})V_{t+2}-2(1-\epsilon_t)V_{t+1}+V_t].\] Retain the omitted remainder and require the negative leading contribution to exceed its magnitude before concluding strict concavity. A model with recovery from incorrect states needs additional terms; the absorbing formula is not a universal replacement.
